properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 6:21PM EST until November 2 at 11:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Palm Beach County, Inland Palm Beach County and
Metro Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- - Pockets of very heavy rainfall resulted in localized flash
flooding on Sunday and earlier today. Forecast amounts look very
similar to yesterday, with common amounts of 1 to 2 inches where
showers and storms occur. Scattered locations around South
Florida may see closer to 2 to 4 inches this evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 10:46AM CST until November 6 at 10:00PM CST by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Quad Cities has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in Iowa...

North Skunk River near Sigourney affecting Keokuk County.

.Potentially heavy rain tonight and Tuesday may produce flooding on
portions of the Skunk River.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...North Skunk River near Sigourney.

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Water affects agricultural land, some
county roads, and farm houses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM CST Monday the stage was 12.6 feet and falling.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached late tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

The next statement will be issued by Tuesday evening.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY EVENING TO FRIDAY EVENING
